rationale: The buyer is a specific, named B2B role — security engineers and CTOs at SaaS companies using third-party auth providers — who already pay for vendor risk management tools (SecurityScorecard, UpGuard, etc.), giving a plausible willingness-to-pay signal. The service can be built as automated monitoring (scraping trust pages, dark-web feeds, HN/Reddit signals, CVE feeds) plus a Claude-powered alert layer with self-serve signup and billing via Stripe, making it largely autonomous once live. The deciding factor holding it at validate rather than build is the absence of any tested responsiveness signal — the WorkOS breach is fresh evidence of pain but no qualified buyers have been probed yet; run 20–30 cold outreach messages to security engineers at auth-dependent SaaS companies before committing to build.
solution_plan: WHAT: A continuous monitoring service that watches your auth/SSO provider (WorkOS, Auth0, Okta, etc.) for breach signals — trust-page changes, dark-web mentions, HN/Reddit alerts, CVE feeds — and notifies you faster than vendor self-disclosure, with a plain-English incident summary. BUILD: The factory sets up scheduled Claude-powered scrapers that poll provider trust pages, security feeds, and social signals; detects anomalies; and drafts breach-summary alerts. A simple landing page with a Stripe subscription ($49–99/month per provider monitored) captures signups. The operator approves the initial outreach batch but does not touch delivery. SELL: Target security engineers and CTOs at Series A–C SaaS companies that list WorkOS, Auth0, or Okta as dependencies — LinkedIn Sales Navigator or GitHub dependency scanning can surface 100+ qualified leads; outreach goes out only after Youval approves. MAINTAIN: Monitoring runs on a cron schedule; alerts are auto-generated by Claude and sent via email/Slack webhook; billing is Stripe recurring; support tickets get a Claude-drafted first response. Only recurring human step is approving outreach batches and reviewing flagged anomalies weekly (~30 min/week). CAVEATS: Signal breadth is limited by what's publicly observable — the service cannot tap private vendor APIs, so some incidents will still be detected late; be transparent about this in marketing.
notes: All build gates pass numerically (operational_autonomy=7 meets floor of 7, buildability=7 meets 6, buyer_clarity=8 meets 6, willingness_to_pay=6 meets 5), but total of 6.3 clears min_total_to_build threshold of 6.5 only marginally — and responsiveness_signal is 2 (untested). Recommend validate stage to run outreach probes before committing to build.
